question.value: What are the magnetic field morphology and strength in the high-mass star forming region G9.62+0.19, and how do they relate to the evolutionary sequence of the cores?

evidence.quote: We aim to determine the magnetic field morphology and strength in the high-mass star forming region G9.62+0.19 to investigate its relation to the evolutionary sequence of the cores.
(Project 2015.1.01349.S, P.I. Wouter Vlemmings)
G9.62 was observed with ALMA in band 7 between 13 May for $\sim$3.5 hours and 27 June 2016 for $\sim$4.5 hours

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: four 2 GHz spectral windows centred at 336.5, 338.5, 348.5, 350.5 GHz, 64 channels each, channel width 31.25 MHz

evidence.quote: The four spectral windows with 2 GHz bandwidth each were centred at 336.5, 338.5, 348.5, and 350.5 GHz and were divided into 64 channels.

evidence.quote: molecular emission was detected from the core MM4a with a peak at 337.6 GHz.

claims.hypothesis: Does magnetic field strength evolve along the core evolutionary sequence?
claims.experiment: DCF and SF field strengths in MM8 (younger) versus MM4 (more evolved)
claims.result: B_SF 17.1 mG for MM8a versus 13.2 mG for MM4
claims.finding: Younger hot core has stronger field than more evolved one

evidence.quote: the less evolved hot core exhibits a stronger magnetic field than the more evolved hot core

claims.hypothesis: Is turbulence or magnetic field dominant in the clump?

evidence.quote: the magnetic energy along the filament appears to dominate over the turbulent energy

claims.experiment: Mass-to-flux ratio from N(H2) and B_SF

evidence.quote: the G9.62 clump appears to be super-critical

claims.hypothesis: Are dust, thermal line and maser field directions consistent?
claims.experiment: Compare dust vectors with rotated line vectors and OH maser data
claims.result: same direction in MM4a; maser comparison only qualitative
